symptom: In a disposable Linux two-process fixture, a Python reader completes real-ancestor lstat checks and blocks before final-component O_NOFOLLOW open. A separate process then replaces the ancestor with a different real directory. The pathname open reads valid decoy JSON while a pre-pinned directory FD reads original JSON; a no-swap control reads original through both. This is a mirrored SDK check/open boundary, not an instrumented live SDK call or production incident.
lesson: Checking each pathname ancestor before opening the final file does not bind the later open to those checked directory objects. O_NOFOLLOW on the final component cannot prevent a real-directory ancestor substitution in the gap. A declared outputDigest field and structurally valid JSON do not authenticate the original pinned publisher object.
guardrail: Reject preflight-only real-ancestor lstat plus final-component O_NOFOLLOW as an atomic reader/writer namespace guarantee. Reuse complete-line process synchronization and the no-swap control; test rename and mount interleavings against an independently reviewed common directory-object authority before considering a new SDK or native bridge. Do not weaken existing symlink guards, auto-delete stale paths, or infer power-loss, production, scoring, or merge readiness.
